WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS  
Connectivity among SAARC Nations  
  *241. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether India has pledged to upgrade connectivity a mong SAARC 
nations; 
(b) whether India has assured SAARC nations that fast a ction would be 
initiated from 1st April, 2007 by making it easier for access to roads and 
transport; 
(c) what other assurances were given by Government at the second SAARC 
Business Leaders Conclave recently; 
(d) whether other SAARC nations have agreed to cooperate; and 
(e) the specific steps assured by other SAARC nations in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI PRANAB 
MUKHERJEE): (a) to (e) Yes, Sir. During the 13th SA ARC Summit held in 
Dhaka in November 2005, Prime Minister had stated that, "If we wish the next 
twenty years of SAARC to be different, we should ta ke the first decision to 
reconnect the countries of the subcontinent on the one hand and then reconnect 
the subcontinent to the larger Asian neighbourhood on the other". We reiterated the 
need for greater connectivity in the South Asian re gion during the Second 
SAARC Business Leaders Conclave held in Mumbai on February 17,2007. 
2. During the upcoming 14th SAARC Summit to be held  in New Delhi on 
April-3-4, 2007, it is proposed to focus on improvi ng infrastructure 
connectivity in the region, particularly in transport, telecommunication and 
2 

[15 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
energy links. It is also proposed to focus on impro ving regional trade through 
improved trade facilitation and increase people-to-people contact among the 
countries in the region. 
3. The need for improved connectivity in the form of t ransport, transit and 
communication links across the region was recognized by the Heads of State and 
Government during the 12th SAARC Summit held in Islamabad and the 13th 
SAARC Summit held in Dhaka in January 2004 and November 2005 respectively. 
All decisions in SAARC are taken on the basis of unanimity. 
4. Government are of the view that if South Asia is to  become a dynamic 
component of the larger process of regional and international cooperation, it must 
bring about economic integration amongst the countr ies in the region. The 
first step towards this, in our view, is to substan tially improve regional 
connectivity. 
Brahmaputra Inland Waterways  
*242. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the time-frame for completion of Talweg Surveys, dr edging etc. for 
implementation of Brahmaputra Inland Waterways in view of his D.O. No. F 
20019/5/2007-MT dated 30.1.2007; 
(b) the percentage of works already completed in view of the two years' time-
frame fixed by IWAI for making National Waterways fully functional; and 
(c) whether Government would consider to constitute a monitoring body with 
the elected representatives of Assam and West Bengal? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI T. R. BAALU): (a) and (b) Regular talweg surveys are being done in the 
National Waterway No. 2(NW-2) from Dhubri to Sadiya on fortnightly basis. In 
alluvial rivers laden with heavy sediment load, which gets deposited in the navigation 
channel thereby reducing depth, regular survey is necessary to ascertain the water 
depth and identify the main channel. Dredging is re quired on shallow patches, 
which forms after every flood season. Presently, dredging in NW-2 is being done with 
the help of one hydraulic surface dredger 
3 

RAJYA SABHA, [15 March, 2007] 
and one cutter suction dredger available with Inland Waterways Authority of India 
(IWAI). Procurement of more dredgers is under process for handling these shallow 
patches timely and more effectively. An Action Plan comprising of 16 projects at an 
estimated cost of Rs. 203.10 crores has been prepared for making the National 
Waterway fully functional. Out of these, 13 projects at an estimated cost of Rs. 
178.25 crores have been sanctioned and are under im plementation. Rs. 18.65 
crores has been spent on these projects till 28th February, 2007. 
(c) There are existing fora which include elected r epresentatives for review 
of Inland Water Transport Sector and it is felt that at present there is no need to 
constitute another committee for monitoring purposes 
Construction of flyover at Badarpur border  
*243. SHRI BASHISTHA NARAIN SINGH: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the construction of a proposed flyov er to be built at T-
junction of Delhi-Faridabad-Jaitpur village (Badarp ur border) at National 
Highway; 
(b) the names of Government and Non-Government agencies involved therein; 
(c) the proposed date of start of construction of the s aid project and the 
projected period of completion; and 
(d) the strategies evolved to complete the proposed project in stipulated time? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI T. R. BAALU): (a) It is proposed to construct  a signal free elevated 
highway including approaches from km 16.100 to km 20.500 on NH-2 (Delhi-
Agra Section) covering 5 major junctions including the T junction of DeIhi-
Faridabad-Jaitpur Village at an estimated cost of Rs, 267 crore. 
(b) The National Highways Authority of India is the implementing agency for the 
above project. The Support Agreement is to be signed by Government of National 
Capital Territory of Delhi and Government of Haryana. The clearances are also 
required from Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Delhi Urban Art Commission 
(DUAC) and Archeological Survey of India (ASI). 
4 

[15 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) and (d) The clearance from the Public-Private P artnership Appraisal 
Committee (PPPAC) has already been obtained for the  project. After getting 
clearance from DDA, DUAC and ASI, the bidding process will be started and 
this process may take three months' time. The selected Concessionaire will have six 
months' time for the financial closure and thirty m onths' time thereafter for 
completion of the project. 
Concern over use of weapons in Space  
†*244. SHRI SHREEGOPAL WAS:                    
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR: 
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state. 
(a) whether Government are concerned over use of weapons in space; 
(b) if so, the measures being taken by Government for shielding against such 
weapons; and 
(c) whether there is any proposal for carrying out deli berations in this 
regard with other countries? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI PRANAB 
MUKHERJEE): (a) The Government are concerned that t he longstanding 
international consensus on peaceful uses of outer s pace might be undermined 
by deployment of weapons in outer space as well as testing and deployment of 
weapons against outer space objects. 
(b) and (c) Government continue to monitor developments on this subject and are 
committed to taking all necessary steps to safeguar d the nation's security in 
accordance with its own assessment. Government continue to be engaged with 
international efforts to keep outer space free of weapons. 
Setting up of National Science and Social Science Foundation  
 *245. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:                      
MS. MABEL REBELLO: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have taken a view on the recommendation of National 
Knowledge Commission regarding setting up of a National Science and Social 
Science Foundation (NSSF);

5 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2007] 
(b) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) if so, the details of the mandate of NSSF; 
(d) what would be the linkages of the new foundation wi th the existing 
network of the research institutions in science and social science; and 
(e) in what manner Government propose to avoid overlap in mandates? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) and (b) Government ha s received the 
Report of the National Knowledge Commission (NKC) on "National Science and 
Social Science Foundation" which has been sent to the Department of Science 
& Technology and Higher Education for their comments. 
(c) The objectives of the National Science and Soci al Science Foundation 
as proposed by National Knowledge Commission are: 
* Suggest policy initiatives to make India a leader in the creation and 
use of new knowledge in all areas of natural, physi cal, agricultural, 
health, and social sciences, with an emphasis on th ose areas which 
cut across traditional disciplines; 
* Ensure that science and technology are maximally us ed.for 
betterment of the lives of our people; 
* Develop a scientific temper. 
(d) and (e) The decision of the Government of India  would take into 
account these issues. 
Issuance of OCI cards  
 †*246. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BALAPTE: 
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR: 
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of OCI cards issued as on date under the  Overseas 
Citizenship of India Scheme; 
(b) the details thereof, country-wise; 
(c) whether Government are planning to formulate any scheme to give special 
facilities to the OCI card holders; and 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

[15 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS (SHRI VAYALAR 
RAVI): (a) to (d) The Overseas Citizenship of India  (OCI) Scheme was 
launched during the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas 2006 at Hyderabad in January, 2006. 
The facility of Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) is given to Persons of Indian 
Origin (PIOs) of all countries [who were citizens of India or eligible to become 
citizens of India on 26th January, 1950 and are citizens of the countries (except 
Pakistan and Bangladesh). As on 10 March, 2007, 1,0 6,945 OCI documents 
have beer, issued to overseas Indians. Country-wise  details are piaced at 
Statement. (See betow) 
Registered OCIs are entitled for life-long, multi-purpose, multi.entry visa to 
visit India. They are also treated at par with Non-Resident indians in the matter of 
inter-country adoption of Indian children; with resident Indian nationals in the 
matter of tariffs in air fares in domestic sectors; and are charged same entry fees 
as domestic Indian visitors'to visit national parks and wildlife sanctuaries in 
India. 
OCI cards holders have been requesting some additio nal benefits as 
available to citizens of India. Government is prese ntly examining these 
requests and would take a view shortly.

Expenditure pattern under Central schemes  
*247 SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) the expenditure pattern under the Central schemes during the Financial 
Year 2006-07, quarter-wise; 
(b) the break-up of revenue and capital expenditures under the Central 
schemes; 
(c) whether it is a fact that the allocations under the Central schemes  have not 
been spent evenly through the Financial Year; 
(d) the schemes that have not been able to use even hal f of the funds till 
December, 2006, Ministry-wise details thereof; and 
(e) the steps that are being taken for a more efficient and even utilization of 
funds of Central schemes? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING ( SHRI 
M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) to (d) The information on M inistry/ 
Department wise actual Plan expenditure upto December, 2006 against Budget 
Estimates (BE) of 2006-07 as brought out in the Con troller General of 
Accounts' (CGA) monthly Bulletin isgiven in the Statement-I and Statement-ll 
(See below). CGA is the principal Accounts Adviser to the Government of 
India and is responsible for establishing and maint aining a technically sound 
management accounting system. It prepares a critica l analysis of expenditures, 
revenues, borrowings and the deficit for Finance Mi nistry every month. 
However, as indicated by CGA, it does not compile C entral Scheme-wise 
accounts of Ministries/  Departments which are bein g maintained by the 
concerned Ministries/ Departments. 
(e) Regular monitoring is done for more efficient and even utilization of funds 
of Central Schemes.

†*248. SHRIMATI SUSHMA SWARAJ: Will the Minister of  URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any scheme has been formulated for the development of famous 
pilgrimage cities under the Jawaharlal Nehru Nation al Urban Renewal

REDDY): (a) and (b) Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban  Renewal Mission 
(JNNURM) was launched on 3-12-2005 to provide refor ms linked central 
assistance to select 63 cities for development of infrastructure, improved service 
delivery including services to urban poor and impro ved urban governance. 
These cities broadly include the followign categories: 
(i) Mega Cities :   7 
(ii) Million-plus cities :   28 
(iii) Selected cities/Urban Agglomerations (UA) (State       :   28 Capitals 
and other cities/UA of religious/historic and touristic importance). 
A list of these 63 cities is given at Statement-I (See below). 
Some of the cities and towns have pilgrimage significance as well. 
Another scheme known as the Urban Infrastructure De velopment Scheme 
for Small & Medium Towns (UIDSSMT) was also launche d simultaneously, 
which also aims at improvement in urban infrastruct ure, improved service 
delivery including services to urban poor and improved urban governance in all 
other towns and cities covered under sub-mission on Urban Infrastructure and 
Governance. 
It is for the State Governments to prioritise pilgr image towns and take up 
development under UIDSSMT.

Statement-II  
Salient features of JNNURM 
Mission Objectives 
• Focussed attention to integrated development of inf rastructural 
services 
• Secure effective linkages between asset creation an d asset 
management 
• Ensure adequate investment of funds to fulfill deficiencies in the urban 
sector. 
• Planned development of identified cities including peri-urban areas, 
out growths, urban corridors, so that urbanization takes placed in a 
dispersed manner. 
• Scale up delivery of civic amenities and provision of utilities with 
emphasis on universal access to urban poor. 
• To take up urban renewal programme, i.e. re-development of inner 
(old) cities areas to reduce congestion. 
Strategy 
• Mission to have two Sub-missions, namely: 
• Urban Infrastructure & Governance under the Ministr y of Urban 
Development 
• Basic Services to the Urban Poor under the Ministry of Housing and 
Urban Poverty Alleviation 
• Reform Linked Central Assistance 
• Identified cities to prepare City Development Plans, Investment Plans 
and Detailed Project Reports to Central Government through the 
State Government. 
• Fund proposed to be released by the Central Governm ent as 
Additional Central Assistance (100% Central Grant) to the State 
Government or its designated State Level agencies.

Cities with 4 million plus population : 07 
Cities with 1 million plus but less than 4 million population : 28 
Selected Cities/Urban Agglomerations (UA) (State Capitals and : 28 other 
cities/UA of religious/historic and touristic importance) 
• Rs. 50,000 crore oyer the Mission period for both  Sub-Missions, 
UIDSSMT and IHSDP has been committed. 
Eligible Sectors 
• Urban Infrastructure and Governance 
a. Urban Renewal 
b. Water Supply including Desaiination Plants and Sewerage 
c. Solid Waste Management 
d. Construction/Improvement of Storm Water Drains 
e. Urban Transport 
f. Parking lots/spaces on Public Private Partnership basis 
g. Development of heritage areas

Hill States 
i. Preservation of Water bodies.

• To improve financial health of the local bodies, su stainability of 
assets created, improvement of urban governance and service delivery, 
reforms have been proposed at State and urban local bodies levels. 
• Reforms are of two categories: mandatory reforms an d optional 
reforms. All reforms have to be completed within th e Mission 
period by the States and ULBs/Parastatals. These are:— 
• Accrual-based double entry system of accounting 
• Introduction of system of e-governance using. IT ap plications like, 
GIS and MIS for various services provided by ULBs.

Salient features of UIDSSMT  
Urban Infrastructure Development Scheme for Small &  Medium Towns 
(UIDSSMT) aim at improvement in urban infrastructure in towns and cities (other 
than the 63 cities identified under JNNURM) in a planned manner. It subsumes 
the existing schemes viz. Integrated Development of Small and Medium 
Towns (IDSMT) and Accelerated Urban Water Supply Pr ogramme 
(AUWSP), The scheme will apply to all cities/towns as per 2001 census, 
excepting cities/towns covered under Jawaharlal Neh ru National Urban 
Renewal Mission (JNNURM). 
Objectives: 
(a) Improve infrastructural facilities and help create durable public assets 
and quality oriented services in cities & towns, 
(b) Enhance public-private-partnership in infrastructural development and 
(c) Promote planned integrated development of towns and cities. 
24 

[15 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
Components: 
The com ponents for assistance under the scheme wil l include all urban 
infrastructure development projects including water supply and sewerage. The 
scheme will cover the following areas: 
* Urban Renewal 
* Water Supply & sanitation 
* Sewerage and solid waste management 
* Construction and improvement of drains/storm water drains 
* Construction/upgradation of roads, highways/expressways 
* Parking lots/spaces on public private partnership basis 
* Development of heritage areas 
* Prevention and rehabilitation of soil erosion/land slides 
Financing Pattern 
 
* The sharing of funds would be in the ratio of 80:10  between 
Central Government and State Government and balance 10% could 
be raised by the nodal agencies from Financial Institutions. 
* Central assistance (grant) is released directly to the nodal agencies 
as Additional Central Assistance (ACA). 
* Central share is released in two instalments depend ing on 
availability of state share and submission of Utili sation certificate 
within 12 months of the closure of the financial year. 
Reforms 
The provision of Central assistance is linked to im plementation of certain 
mandatory as well as optional reforms at the State and ULB/Para-statal levels. 
Implementation of all mandatory and optional reform s has to be completed 
during the Mission period.

†*249. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA: Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that several cyber cafes are misusing internet services 
by putting obscene pictures and informations in websites; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
25 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2007] 
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that one website h ad recently shown 
obscene picture of Mahatma Gandhi; 
(c) whether Government would take some steps to check m isuse of 
websites and cyber crimes as well; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN): (a) The National  Crime 
Records Bureau (NCRB), maintains national crime data. During the year 2005, 
88 cases of obscene publication/transmission in ele ctronics form were 
registered in various states under Section 67 of th e Information Technology 
Act, 2000. However, NCRB does not maintain specific  information regarding 
such misuse of Internet services by the cyber cafes. 
(b) to (d) A website by the name 'www.youtube.com' has hosted some 
objectionable content regarding Mahatma Gandhi. This said website is hosted 
on servers in United States of America. Information  Technology Act, 2000 
together with Indian Penal Code provides a legal framework to check misuse of 
websites and cyber crimes in India. 
A Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on 15.12.2006 to further strengthen the 
provisions of the Information Technology Act, 2000. The Bill inter-alia provides 
for cyber crimes like publishing of material containing sexually explicit act in 
electronic form, e-commerce frauds through impersonation commonly known 
as phishing, identity theft and pffensive messages through communication 
service. 
However, the websites hosted on the servers abroad are subject to the laws of 
those countries. This poses technological as well as legal issues in taking action 
against such websites.

Safety audit in coal mines  
1808. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether safety audit is periodically carried out in respect of coal mines 
operating under Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. (BCCL) and others; 
(b) if so, whether over 50 per cent of the coal mines operating under BCCL 
and other have been declared unsafe for operating; 
(c) if so, the details of the coal mines so declared unsafe; and 
(d) the steps taken to provide due safety to workers wo rking in these 
collieries? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (DR. DASARI 
NARAYANA RAO): (a) Safety audit in Bharat Coking Co al Ltd. and other 
subsidiary companies of Coal India Ltd. is conducted periodically. 
(b) No, Sir. Mining operations are carried out in Coal mines of Bharat 
Coking Coal Ltd. (BCCL) and other subsidiary compan ies of Coal India Ltd. 
(CIL) in accordance with the Statutes under Mines A ct 1952 and rules and 
regulations framed there under such as Coal Mines Regulations 1957, Mines Rules 
1955 etc. and circulars issued from time to time by Directorate General of Mines 
Safety (DGMS). Permissions are obtained from DGMS w herever necessary. 
However, if violations are pointed out during the course of inspections by the 
officials of DGMS, immediate action is taken by off icials of mines to rectify 
the violations. In addition, officers of Internal Safety Organizations of subsidiary 
companies also carry regular inspection of mines to monitor safety of mines and 
persons working therein. 
(c) Does not arise in view of reply given to part (b) above. 
(d) Following broad safety measures are being adopted by CIL to provide due 
safety to the workers: 
1. CIL has established a structured multi-disciplin ary Internal Safety 
Organisation (ISO) to assist the line management at  various levels 
in matters related to safety. 
46 

[15 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
2. Conducting Safety Audit of mines by experts for assessment of threats 
and implementation of the recommendations thereof once every 2 years 
or earlier if necessary. 
3. Introduction of Risk Assessment as a tool for impro vement of 
safety—Risk assessment has been conducted in some m ines in each 
coal producing mines of C.I.L. 
4. Thrust is being maintained on preparedness for emer gencies 
through: 
 
(a) Reviewing emergency action plans for each and every  district in 
underground. 
(b) Demarcating escape routes on plans as well as in working areas below 
ground. 
(c) Conducting mock rehearsals and monitoring failure p oints for 
further improvement. 
5. Towards avoidance of accident due to inundation the following 
measures are being taken: 
(a) Taking the required preventive measures against dan ger of 
inundation after assessment of danger from under ground and surface 
source of water in each mine prior to every monsoon. 
(b) Conducting check surveys by company surveyors as we ll as cross 
checking the same in some cases by external agencies. 
(c) Establishment of centralized emergency pumping arrangement for use 
during emergencies. 
6. Thrust on measures for reduction of roof and sid e-fall accidents 
in below ground mines are being continued by: 
(a) Drawing up of support plans based on RMR and implementation of the 
same. 
(b) Greater use of Roof Bolting/Stitching methods of roof support by quick 
setting cement capsuies. 
(c) Introduction of mechanized drilling by roof bolting  machines 
thereby 
(i) improving quality of roof bolting as weil as 
47 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2007] 
(ii) reducing exposure of roof bolting crew to hazard of roof fall 
(d) Introduction of resin grouted roof bolts in water seams. 
(e) Training of support personnel and Supervisors. 
(f) Reducing exposure of workman by increasing mech anization 
through SDLs/LHDs, PSLW and continuous miners. 
(7) Measures for reduction of accidents in open cast mines were pursued through 
(a) Implementation of various Codes of practices, Traff ic Rules, 
Checking of contractor's vehicles/equipment by comp any 
engineers. 
(b) Training of Heavy Earth Moving Machinery operators and 
contractor workers. 
(c) Enhancement of safety awareness through publicity a nd 
propaganda, safety drives, safety weeks etc. 
8. Thrust on training and retraining of workmen, supervisors to increase safety 
awareness of the workmen. CIL is preparing training films on CD for imparting 
standardized training in all its training centers.

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2007] 
The Ministers discussed the political, security and economic aspects of the 
current global situation, besides exchanging views on how international 
relations are being presently conducted. They noted  that globalization opens 
up opportunities for a more even distribution of de velopment resources and 
influence in the world thus creating a foundation for a more stable and balanced 
international system. They also emphasized the need to preserve the cultural and 
civilizational diversity of the contemporary world and to promote the existing 
initiatives for dialogue among civilizations and religions. They expressed their 
conviction that democratization of international re lations is the key to 
building an increasingly multi-polar world order th at would be based on 
principles of equality of nations - big or small, r espect for sovereignty and 
territorial integrity of countries, international l aw and mutual respect. The 
Ministers acknowledged that the UN is an appropriate instrument for promoting 
and attaining such a world order. The Sides stressed the importance of reforms at 
the UN, including the UN Security Council, in order  to deal with the myriad 
challenges of today's world more effectively. They shared the view that member 
states should aim to make the UN more transparent, efficient and reflective of 
contemporary realities. The Sides agreed to take steps in this direction. In this 
context, the Foreign Ministers of Russia and China reiterated that their 
countries attach great importance to the status of India in international affairs, 
and understand and support India's aspirations to play a greater role in the United 
Nations. 
The Ministers noted that international terrorism co ntinued to pose a grave 
threat to all nations and expressed concern about t he new and evolving forms 
of the menace. They agreed that under central and c oordinating role of the UN 
and within the framework of its Global Counter-Terr orism Strategy collective 
action must be strengthened further by taking into account the mutating character 
of terrorism and its networks, They agreed that an early entry into force of 
International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism and 
the earliest possible adoption in the UN of the Ind ia-sponsored draft 
Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism  would lead to further 
consolidation of the international legal basis for combating terrorism. The Sides 
underlined the substantial of their counter-terrori sm cooperation in regional 
organizations. They agreed that there can be no jus tification for any act of 
terrorism, irrespective of motivations, wherever and by whosoever committed. 
They stressed that 
96 

[15 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
selective approaches in counter-terrorism cannot yield sustainable results and it 
should be combated in consistent, sustained and comprehensive manner without 
any double standards. The Sides also agreed to coordinate action against all factors 
that feed international terrorism, including its financing, illegal drug trafficking 
and trans-national organized crime. 
The Ministers agreed that India, Russia and China, as countries with 
growing international influence, can make substantive positive contribution to 
global peace, security and stability. In this conte xt, the Ministers exchanged 
views on various regional and international issues of concern. They agreed that 
cooperation rather than confrontation should govern approaches to regional and 
global affairs. While welcoming India's joining the  Shanghai Cooperation 
Organization (SCO) as an observer country, the Foreign Ministers of Russia and 
China stated that they would actively facilitate ea rly realization of mutually 
beneficial contribution of India to the SCO 
The Ministers paid specific attention to the high p otential of trilateral 
cooperation and synergy in the economic field. The Ministers reiterated the 
considerable potential for mutually beneficial economic interaction among the 
three countries in areas such as energy, transport infrastructure, health, high 
technologies, including IT and biotechnology. Recognizing the important role 
of the business and industrial circles of the three  consistently growing and 
large economies, the Ministers agreed to advice their respective apex business 
bodies to organize a trilateral business forum taki ng into account the 
capabilities and potential of the three countries. The Ministers agreed to 
monitor this process with a view to facilitating th e agreed business meeting 
which would take place during 2007. 
The Ministers expressed satisfaction at the results of the trilateral meeting in New 
Delhi and agreed to hold their next meeting in China.

Statement-I 
Salient features and Genesis of lHSDP and BSUP under JNNURM  
(I) Integrated Housing & Slum Development (IHSDP): 
For cities/towns not covered under JNNURM, Integrat ed Housing & Slum 
Development (IHSDP) has also been launched along wi th JNNURM on 
3.12.2005. The existing Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana (VAMBAY) and the 
discontinued National Slum Development Scheme (NSDP) are subsumed in the 
IHSDP The IHSDP has been launched with the objective to strive for holistic slum 
development, with a healthy and enabling urban envi ronment by providing 
adequate shelter and basic infrastructure facilties to the slum dwellers of the 
identified'urban areas. 
Salient features of IHSDP 
> Central Assistance in the form of ACA as full grant " 
> 80% of the project cost borne by the Central Government 
> 90% of the project cost borne by the Central Government for projects from 
cities/towns in special category States. 
> A minimum of 12% beneficiary contribution for house s. For SC/ST/ 
BC/OBC/PH and other weaker sections, 10% beneficiar y 
contribution. 
102 

[15 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
> Access of Centra; assistance predicated upon the State/Urban Local 
Bodies/Parastatals agreeing to the reforms. 
> Reforms to ensure imrovement in urban Governance. 
> Cities/towns to prepare Detailed Project Reports.  
Admissible Components under IHSDP: 
(i) Provision of shelter including upgradation & co nstruction of new 
houses. 
  Provision of community toilets. 
(iii) Provision of physical amenties like water sup ply, storm water 
drains, community bath, widening and paving of exis ting lanes, 
sewers, community latrines, street lights, etc. 
(iv) Community Infrastructure like provision of community centres to be 
used for pre-school education, non-formal education , adult 
education, recreational activities, etc. 
(v) Community Primary Health Care Centre Buildings can be 
provided. 
(vi) Social Amenties like pre-school education, non-formal education, adult 
education, maternity, child health and Primary health care including 
immunization, etc. 
(vii) Provision of Model Demonstration Projects. 
(viii) Sites and Services/houses at affordable cost s for EWS & LIG 
categories. 
(ix) Slum improvement and rehabilitation projects. 
(x) Land acquisition cost will not be financed exce pt for acquision of 
private land for schemes/projects in the North Eastern States & hilly 
States, viz., Himachal Pradesh, Uttaranchai and Jammu & Kashmir. 
(II) Basic Services to the Uraban Poor (BSUP) under JNNURM: 
Cities and towns of India constitute the world's second largest urban system. 
They contribute over 50% of country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and are 
central to economic growth. For these cities to rea lize their full potential and 
become true engines of growth, it is necessary that 
103 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2007] 
focused attention be given to the improvement of in frastructure therein. For 
achieving this objective, a Mission mode approach i s essential. Accordingly, 
the Hon'ble Prime Minister has launched a Mission named Jawahar Lal Nehru 
National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) on 3rd Dece mber, 2005. The 
Mission comprises two Sub-Missions — one for Basic Services to the Urban Poor 
(BSUP) and the other for Infrastructure and Governance. The JNNURM will be 
implemented in select 63 cities. The duration of th e Mission is for 7 years 
beginning from the year 2005-06. 
Salient features of BSUP: 
> The Sub-Mission is to be implemented in 63 select JNNURM cities. 
> To be implemented over 7 years beginning with the year 2005-06. 
> Central Assistance in the form of ACA as full grant. 
> 50% percent of the project cost in respect of cities having million plus 
population or above to be borne by the Central Government. 
> 90% of the project cost borne by the Central Government for projects from 
cities/towns in North Eastern States and Jammu & Kashmir. 
> 80% of the project cost borne by the Central Government for projects from 
the remaining cities. 
>  A minimum of 12% beneficiary contribution for houses. For SC/ST/ 
BC/OBC/PH and other weaker sections, 10% beneficiary 
contribution. 
> Access of Central assistance predicated upon the State/Urban Local 
Bodies/Parastatals agreeing to the reforms. 
> Reforms to ensure improvement in urban Governance. 
> Cities to prepare City Developmnent Plans and Detailed project 
Reports. 
Admissible Components under BSUP: 
i.  Integrated development of slums, i.e., housing and development of 
infrastructure projects in the slums in the identified cities. 
ii. Projects involving development/improvement/maintenance of basic 
services to the urban poor.

iii. Slum improvement and rehabilitation projects. 
iv. Projects on water supply/sewerage/drainage, community toilets/ baths, 
etc. 
v.  Houses at affordable costs for slum dwellers/urban poor/EWS/ LIG 
categories. 
vi. Construction and improvements of drains/storm water drains. 
vii. Environmental improvement of slums and solid waste 
management. 
viii. Street lighting. 
ix. Civic amenities, like, community halls, child care centres, etc. 
x. Operation and maintenance of assets created under this component. 
xi. Convergence of health, education and social security schemes for the 
urban poor.

The National Knowledge Commission submits its recommendations in the 
form of letters to the Prime Minister on specific issues under its mandate. So far NKC 
has submitted 11 sets of recommendations as follows:

*Re-engineer government processes first, to change our basic governance pattern

governance. 
*Select 10 to 20 important services that make a cri tical difference, 
simplify them and offer then as web-based services. 
*Begin all new national programmes (like Bharat Nir man, Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme, etc.) with well-engine ered e-govemance 
implementation and web interface. 
2. Translation (1 September 2006) 
*Provide impetus for developing translation as an industry 
*Establish a store-house of information on all aspe cts of translation 
involving Indian languages 
*Promote printed as well as virtual publication of translation studies 
*Create and maintain various tools for translation,  encourage machine 
translation 
*Provide quality training and education for translators 
*Translate pedagogic materials at all level specifically in natural and social 
sciences

*Project Indian languages and literatures through high-quality translation *Set 
up a national web portal on translation *Organize Annual National 
Conferences on Translation *Promote book launches, festivals, fellowships 
and prizes etc. *Set up a Mission on Translation for this purpose 
3. Language (20 October 2006) 
*Introduce English, along with the first language s tarting from Class I in 
school 
*Modify pedagogy of language learning/teaching redu cing 
disproportionate emphasis on grammar and rules 
*Train the nearly four million school teachers all over the country, 
regardless of their subject expertise, especially at the primary level, to improve 
their proficiency in English through vacation training programmes or other short-
term courses 
*Induct graduates with high proficiency in English and good 
communication skills without formal teacher-training qualifications through an 
appropriate procedure 
*Develop pedagogically sound English textbooks for every level, from Class 
I to XII. These should be used as models by states. 
*Create langauge learning opportunities inside and outside the class room 
using all available media-audio-visual, print etc. 
4. Right to Education (23 October 2006) 
*A legislation on Right to Education must be enforc ed by the central 
government following upon the commitment made in th e Constitutional 
Amendment Article 21A 
*There must be financial provision in the central l egislation, requiring the 
central government to provide the bulk of the additional funds required to ensure 
the Right to Education 
*The responsibility of the Governmetn, at different  levels, must be 
recognized and made justiciable

2006)

will look at all knowledge as one seamless entity

—suggest policy initiatives to make India a leader in the creation and use of 
new knowledge in all areas of natural, physical, agricultural, health, and social 
sciences, with emphasis on those areas which cut ac ross traditional

introduce course credit system, enhance reliance on  internal assessment,

upgradation of infrastructure, salary differentials etc. 
*Ensure access for all deserving students through w ell funded 
scholarships and affirmative action that take into account multi 
dimensionality of deprivation

*Place Vocational Education entirely under the Mini stry of Human 
Resource Development

education system

*Enhance the training options available for the unorganized and informal sector

High cost of ship-berthing in India ports 
1906. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is fact that as appeared in print media that, it costs a container ship 
US$ 32,000 per day to use a port in India; 
(b) if so, the reasons for this high cost of berthing of ships in Indian ports; 
(c) the steps that would be taken to reduce the cost of berthing in Indian ports; 
(d) whether it is also a fact that the turn around time for an average ship is 11.9 days; 
and 
(e) the steps proposed to import port management in India? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU): (a) to (c) Major Port Trusts collect vessel related charges as per the Scale of 
Rates notified by the Tariff Authority for Major Ports (TAMP) from time to time. The 
prevailing berth hire charges in major ports for container ships varies from US$ 0.00195 per 
Gross Registered Tonnage (GRT) per hour to US$ 0.0096" per GRT per hour. The actual 
payment to ports, therefore, varies with the GRT of the ship and its duration of stay at the port. 
The scale of rates is notified by TAMP following a cost plus minimum return on capital 
employed model. All vessel related charges including berth hire charges at Jawaharial Nehru 
Port, which handled about 60% of container traffic of the country, has been reduced by 30% in 
October, 2006. 
(d) The turn round time of vessels in the major ports varied from 4.39 days to 1.96 days 
in 2005-06. The average turn round time of vessel calling at all major ports was 3.5 days 
for the year 2005-06. 
(e) Improvement of port management is an ongoing process. This entails modernisation of 
equipments, mechanization of cargo handling, training of workforce, electronic data 
interchange, internal computerization of ports, development of Port Community 
System etc.

these requests, the Ministry took up the matter wit h the Planning 
Commission and Ministry of Finance for reviewing th e decision in view of 
financial constraints of States, cost intensive nat ure of certain categories 
of infrastructure such as synthetic surfaces etc., and the committed liability 
towards the approved projects. The Planning Commiss ion did not agree to 
the request stating that these schemes were identif ied for transfer to states 
as part of the general exercise to reduce the numbe r of centrally sponsored 
schemes, but agreed to provide funds for completion  of ongoing projects 
during the 10th Plan to the extent of the committed liability.

rural areas, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Spor ts is considering the 
launching of a scheme—"Panchayat Yuva Khel Abhiyan"  with the objective

activities, at the village/sub-district level, both as an essential ingredient of the 
development of the youth and to significantly expand the catchment for spotting 
and nurturing of sports talent. Consultations are being held in this regard with all 
the stakeholders concerned with a view to finalizing the proposal.
